protocol.py: 15 biology problems (4 errors, 7 warnings, 4 notes).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 12 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 63:  p300.aspirate(12, components_rack["A3"])
   At line 63 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 12 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul. A
   pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and
   the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells:
   tube A3 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A3 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [23823c6e3fec]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 6: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 92:  p300.aspirate(23, master_reservoir["A1"])
   At line 92 the p300_single_gen2 draws 23 ul from well A1 in slot 6 with its tip 1 mm
   above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 184 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well
   Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.87 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this
   line did it 8 times, after 40 times in the liquid; 184 ul of air in all). The simulator
   does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 8 wells filled from these draws got
   air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 6.
   Also reached 8 other wells: wells D5, D6, D7, D8, D9, D10, D11 and D12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: 12 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
findings.explanation: At line 63 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 12 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul. A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: tube A3 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 6: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 92 the p300_single_gen2 draws 23 ul from well A1 in slot 6 with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 184 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.87 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 8 times, after 40 times in the liquid; 184 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 8 wells filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 47 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 39 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 92. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: dntp (tube A2 in slot 2)
findings.explanation: At line 59 the tip went into dntp (tube A2 in slot 2) while it still carried buffer (tube A1 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 8 other wells: wells D5, D6, D7, D8, D9, D10, D11 and D12 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 59 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 92 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 6 while it still carried template 1 (tube A1 in slot 4), template 2 (tube A2 in slot 4), template 3 (tube A3 in slot 4), template 4 (tube A4 in slot 4) and 35 more from an earlier step (this line did it 39 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 47 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 39 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 92, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: No no-template control: 40 wells of dntp and polymerase with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 94 the robot starts putting dntp and polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 3), and 40 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 32 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.75 ul of dntp and polymerase and 2 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 40 wells never mixed after template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 36 more went in (8% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 105 the robot added template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 36 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 32 more in slot 3, which already held buffer, dntp, polymerase, fwd primer and 2 more (this line did it 40 times). The addition was 8% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 32 more in slot 3 after line 105: `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
